nodes.name: One-step pyrolysis with HCl
nodes.procedure: RhP₂/Rh@NPG was synthesized by pyrolyzing a mixture of melamine, glyphosate, and RhCl₃ with addition of HCl to the homogeneous precursor mixture, which assists the self-assembly of the small molecules into a supermolecule-like structure by linking the small molecules by Cl⁻ and H⁺. Then, Rh³⁺ ions are trapped in the open spaces of the supermolecule-like structure. During the pyrolysis, the Rh³⁺ ions near or binded to glyphosate react with the highly reactive P atoms to form RhP₂, whereas the other Rh³⁺ ions are reduced to metallic Rh. The small molecules are then carbonized to afford RhP₂/Rh heterojunction nanoparticles embedded in N,P co-doped graphene.
nodes.source_text: RhP₂/Rh@NPG was synthesized by pyrolyzing a mixture of melamine, glyphosate, and RhCl₃. As shown in Figure 1, the difference between the synthesis routes for RhP₂/Rh@NPG and RhP₂@NPG is the addition of HCl to the homogeneous precursor mixture...

nodes.name: One-step pyrolysis without HCl
nodes.procedure: In the thermal polymerization procedure without HCl, the homogeneous melamine, glyphosate, and Rh³⁺ ions react to form RhP₂ nanoparticles embedded in N,P co-doped graphene (RhP₂@NPG).
nodes.source_text: In contrast, in the thermal polymerization procedure without HCl, the homogeneous melamine, glyphosate, and Rh³⁺ ions react to form RhP₂ nanoparticles embedded in N,P co-doped graphene (RhP₂@NPG)...

nodes.name: Pyrolysis with L-alanine substitution
nodes.procedure: For comparison, metallic Rh nanoparticles embedded in N-doped graphene (Rh@NG) were prepared by replacing glyphosate with L-alanine in the synthesis.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, we also prepared metallic Rh nanoparticles embedded in N-doped graphene (Rh@NG) by replacing glyphosate with L-alanine in the synthesis.

nodes.name: Calcination for active site identification
nodes.procedure: To identify the active species responsible for HER in RhP₂/Rh@NPG, it was calcined at 950°C for 1 h in Ar atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: To identify the active species responsible for HER in RhP₂/Rh@NPG, it was calcined at 950°C for 1 h in Ar atmosphere.

nodes.characterization_summary: RhP₂/Rh@NPG displays a mixed phase of monoclinic RhP₂ (JCPDS No. 65-1272) and cubic Rh (JCPDS No. 01-1213) with weaker and wider graphitic carbon (002) peak at ≈24.1° indicating poorer crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, RhP₂ / Rh@NPG displays a mixed phase of monoclinic RhP₂ (JCPDS No. 65-1272) and cubic Rh (JCPDS No. 01-1213).

nodes.characterization_summary: RhP₂/Rh@NPG has Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface area of 913.4 m²g⁻¹, RhP₂@NPG 878.4 m²g⁻¹, and Rh@NG 378.3 m²g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b and Figure S4 (Supporting Information) show the nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherms and the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface area for RhP₂ / Rh@NPG, RhP₂@NPG, and Rh@NG were 913.4, 878.4, and 378.3 m²g⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: RhP₂/Rh@NPG has uniformly distributed nanoparticles averaging 2.45 nm diameter on graphene; RhP₂@NPG averages 4.19 nm and Rh@NG 9.58 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, RhP₂ / Rh@NPG has uniformly distributed nanoparticles with an average diameter of ≈2.45 nm on graphene (inset in Figure 2c), which are smaller than those in RhP₂@NPG (≈4.19 nm) and Rh@NG (≈9.58 nm) (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM of RhP₂/Rh@NPG shows nanoparticles with high crystallinity region (Rh(111) 0.22 nm, Rh(200) 0.19 nm) and low crystallinity monoclinic RhP₂ region.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) images (Figure 2d-f) of RhP₂ / Rh@NPG show that the nanoparticles have two different parts—one region with high crystallinity (bright blue area) and the other region with low crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Dark-field TEM and EDS elemental mappings show Rh and P evenly distributed throughout nanoparticles of both RhP₂/Rh@NPG and RhP₂@NPG.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy measurements and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mappings indicate that P and Rh are evenly distributed in the nanoparticles of RhP₂ / Rh@NPG (Figure 2g) and RhP₂@NPG (Figure S9b-d, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Rh 3d XPS of RhP₂/Rh@NPG shows Rh⁰ at 307.2/311.9 eV and Rh⁴⁺ at 308.2/312.9 eV with positive shift of Rh⁰ (0.3 eV) and negative shift of Rh⁴⁺ (0.2 eV) vs RhP₂@NPG indicating electron transfer from Rh⁰ to RhP₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For RhP₂ / Rh@NPG, the peaks at ≈307.2 and ≈311.9 eV are ascribed to metallic Rh⁰ 3d₅/₂ and 3d₃/₂, and those at ≈308.2 and ≈312.9 eV are attributed to Rh⁴⁺ 3d₅/₂ and 3d₃/₂, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Rh K-edge XANES of RhP₂/Rh@NPG shows absorption edge between Rh@NG and RhP₂@NPG with slightly lower rising edge than RhP₂@NPG indicating lower average oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Rh K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra showed that the absorption edge of Rh of RhP₂ / Rh@NPG is located between that of Rh@NG and RhP₂@NPG.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Rh-P scattering at ≈1.8 Å and Rh-Rh at ≈2.4-2.7 Å for RhP₂/Rh@NPG; R_Rh-Rh close to metallic Rh and higher intensity confirms coexistence of metallic Rh⁰ and RhP₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic XANES and FT-EXAFS spectra of RhP₂ / Rh@NPG confirm that both metallic Rh⁰ and RhP₂ coexist in RhP₂ / Rh@NPG.

nodes.characterization_summary: RhP₂/Rh@NPG shows higher D-to-G band intensity ratio than Rh@NG and RhP₂@NPG, consistent with poorer crystallinity and richer defects in carbon substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the diffraction peak at ≈24.1° corresponding to the graphitic carbon (002) plane of RhP₂ / Rh@NPG is weaker and wider. This indicates poorer crystallinity and richer defects in the carbon substrate of RhP₂ / Rh@NPG than those of Rh@NG and RhP₂@NPG, which is consistent with the higher intensity ratio of D-to-G band in the Raman spectrum of RhP₂ / Rh@NPG (Figure S3b, Supporting Information).
